citation.note: Written notice at hire of the rate of pay, day, hour, and place of payment (§ 21-5-9(1)); written notice of any pay-rate or wage-arrangement change at least 1 full pay period prior to the effective date (§ 21-5-9(4)); failure to provide advance notice triggers mandatory reimbursement of the reduction amount on the initial paycheck.

Payroll records retention (2 years minimum): the employer must retain employee name, address, rate of pay, hours worked, payroll deductions, and pay-period amounts for at least 2 years (§ 21-5C-5), kept at the place of employment and made available to the Commissioner of Labor for inspection.
Enforce § 21-5-3 semi-monthly requirement: Ensure the new pay schedule pays wages at least twice per calendar month with no more than 19 days between paydays.
Final pay must be due on or before the next regular payday (§ 21-5-4); employers who fail to pay as required are liable for 2x the unpaid amount in liquidated damages (§ 21-5-4(e)).
